# Portable v0.11 validation

Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -B tools/run_claim_ledger_validation.py`.
This is the single current-release aggregate. It verifies the selected source
manifest, explicit allowed inherited changes, byte-preserved arithmetic/runtime
modules, fourteen exact prior tool definitions and corrected lab modules.

Only embedded pinned source archives supply historical dependencies. In fresh
temporary directories the aggregate reruns the full frozen v0.10 aggregate and
original accepted lab author aggregate plus separately implemented BFS reviewer in
normal and optimized modes. No historical result JSON is treated as execution.
The lab review covers all 543 labeled four-node DAGs with withdrawal subsets and
replacement-withdrawal states, seeded mixed histories, adversarial raw inputs and
semantic source-mutation controls. This is bounded software evidence, not a proof
of implementation correctness or a theorem-validation claim.

The integrated complete test suite runs normally and with Python optimization.
New checks exercise all author fixtures, detached inputs/results, strict Unicode
keys, JSON rejection, CLI exact/over byte bounds, bridge 64 KiB/1 MiB limits,
no extra capability arguments, no proof/truth promotion, stateless errors and
preserved runtime registry. Current inherited integration, arithmetic, mutation
and preinstalled optional schema audits are also rerun. A new independently
authored integration review is mandatory in both modes. The fourteen-tool
subprocess differential checks positive and malformed calls against embedded
v0.10 and compares full responses, not only tool counts.

`python -B tools/reproduce_claim_ledger_release.py` builds the ZIP twice, checks
identical bytes and fixed metadata, extracts only SOURCE-MANIFEST.json plus its
explicit named files, runs the aggregate in normal and optimized processes, compares
results, rebuilds identical ZIP bytes, and verifies source-drift rejection. No
sibling trees are consulted. Generated evidence is excluded from the shipped
selection and regenerated in the extraction. Embedded reviewed archives contain
historical evidence for provenance only; executable replay never uses it as a pass.

The explicit baseline changes are limited to README/provenance/release selection,
CLI dispatch, bridge version/import/dispatch/tool append, inventory expectations
and the portable test module copy list. No inherited arithmetic engine or runtime
acceptance registry changes. New source and independent review files are additional.
Fixed hashes identify bytes, not authenticity. Lean remains an explicit unavailable
skip when not installed; no installation is attempted. No repository publication,
actual HM data, network, external models or live proof execution is involved.
